plain_english: May we see the deep — circled by supreme light, its darkness wiped, lovely — and dwell within your cave.
sanskrit_cite: api paśyema gambhīrāṃ pareṇa jyotiṣābhitaḥ unmṛṣṭatamasaṃ ramyām antarbhava bhavadguhām

plain_english: Homage to them even — who see the moon-crested lord, giver of supreme bliss, even in dream.
sanskrit_cite: namas tebhyo 'pi ye somakalākalitaśekharam nāthaṃ svapne 'pi paśyanti paramānandadāyinam

plain_english: O Blessed — be! — the desire to contemplate your-ish being, skilled at cutting rebirth-fear: to whom is it not pleasing?
sanskrit_cite: bhagavan bhava bhāvatkaṃ bhāvaṃ bhāvayituṃ ruciḥ punarbhavabhayocchedadakṣā kasmai na rocate

plain_english: Lifelong, O world-lord, let this be our task: staying, by your grace, with mind single-pointed on you alone.
sanskrit_cite: yāvajjīvaṃ jagannātha kartavyam idam astu naḥ tvatprasādāt tvadekāgramanaskatvena yā sthitiḥ

plain_english: To the self made of thousand-branch-spread Veda and Āgama: bow; to Śambhu, the wish-tree of endless fruit.
Having entrusted speech, mind, body's acts in you, O Lord — become you-made, pair-free: may we be, at any time?
sanskrit_cite: vāṅmanaḥkāyakarmāṇi viniyojya tvayi prabho tvanmayībhūya nirdvandvāḥ kaccit syāmāpi karhicit

plain_english: In the creation-and-dissolution appointments for each welfare of worlds — to the independently powerful, to the trident-bearer: bow.
Of the chief meditation-object past guṇa-yoga, of Dhūrjaṭi — even the name: for meditators, by meditations, what fruit by other supports?
sanskrit_cite: vyatītaguṇayogasya mukhyadhyeyasya dhūrjaṭeḥ nāmāpi dhyāyatāṃ dhyānaiḥ kim anyālambanaiḥ phalam

plain_english: Bow, bow — 'to Śiva' thus said: by mantra-power taking refuge, praiseworthy they who strive to enjoy Śāmbhavī fortune.
sanskrit_cite: namo namaḥ śivāyeti mantrasāmarthyam āśritāḥ ślāghyās te śāmbhavīṃ bhūtim upabhoktuṃ ya udyatāḥ

plain_english: What path by which unattainable? What speech by which unspoken? What meditation by which unmeditated? What — what are you not, O Lord?
sanskrit_cite: kaḥ panthā yena na prāpyaḥ kā ca vāṅ nocyase yayā kiṃ dhyānaṃ yena na dhyeyaḥ kiṃ vā kiṃ nāsi yat prabho
